mainTopic: The source for לב בית דין מתנה, what רבי שמעון does with leftover תמיד lambs, and the גזירה against offering a former חטאת as an עולה
overview: The גמרא is looking for a תנא who holds that the בית דין silently sets conditions on הקדש even for something that rarely happens. It tries three sources: the רבנן of קטורת, the רבנן of פרה אדומה, and the speakers of "אמרו לו" in the משנה. Each one is pushed aside. Incense cannot be left to graze, a פרה is very expensive, and the "אמרו לו" speaker might be רבי מאיר, who allows swapping the goats for a different reason. So the גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן simply learned the dispute as a tradition. רבי יוחנן then explains that for רבי שמעון the leftover תמיד lambs are offered as filler offerings for the מזבח. רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק adds that leftover חטאת goats are not offered themselves; only their value is used, because of a גזירה made after atonement on account of before atonement. אביי, רבא and רבינא each bring a source supporting this גזירה, and the גמרא accepts it. Finally, a ברייתא is opened that asks what is brought from the leftover lambs, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Incense is different: it cannot be left to graze
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the רבנן of קטורת is rejected, because incense has no other fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: Incense is different, because it is not something that can be sent out to graze!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the case of leftover קטורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a leftover animal, there is a backup plan: let it graze until it gets a מום, then redeem it. Incense has no such backup plan. So even someone who normally says the court does not set conditions for rare cases might agree it does for קטורת.

keyTerms.meaning: is different
the incense offered in the בית המקדש
something that can be put out to graze (until it gets a blemish)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the court never sets conditions. It is only saying the קטורת case cannot prove the rule for rare cases, because incense has no other solution.

phrases.english: Incense is different
since it is not something that can graze!
phrases.notes: With animals you can wait for a blemish and then redeem them. You can't do that with incense.

steps.triggerLanguage: שאני קטורת דלא בר רעיה היא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earlier suggestion that the רבנן of קטורת are the source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the רבנן of קטורת only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Incense has no other fix (it cannot graze), so it may be a special case.

steps.title: Suggesting the רבנן of the red heifer
steps.stepSummary: New suggestion: the source is the רבנן who allow redeeming a פרה אדומה if a better one is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it is the רבנן of the פרה case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new candidate: the רבנן who say a פרה אדומה can be redeemed when a better one turns up. This line only sets up the suggestion; the next line tests it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Finding a better פרה is uncommon. If the court still sets a condition so the first one can be redeemed, that suggests these רבנן hold the court sets conditions even for rare cases.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (switching to a new suggestion)
the red heifer

phrases.english: Rather, the Rabbis of the heifer case
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא brought earlier: if a choicer heifer is found, the first may be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קטורת proof failed, offers a replacement source.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנא holds לב בית דין מתנה even for uncommon cases.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רבנן who allow redeeming a פרה אדומה when a choicer one is found.

steps.title: The heifer is different: it is very expensive
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: maybe the court sets a condition on a פרה only because of its high price.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps a פרה is different, because its price is high!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the פרה proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרה אדומה costs a fortune. Maybe the court sets a condition even for this rare case only to avoid a huge loss. That would not prove the rule for ordinary items.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps
its price is high

phrases.english: Perhaps the heifer is different
since its price is high!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the proof suggested in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the רבנן of פרה only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The heifer's great value may be the special reason for the condition.

steps.title: Suggesting the רבנן of "they said to him"
steps.stepSummary: Third suggestion: the רבנן introduced with "אמרו לו" in the משנה on 2b.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it is the רבנן of "they said to him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third candidate: the רבנן who answer רבי שמעון in the משנה with "אמרו לו." This line sets up the suggestion, and the next line will question it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, the speakers ask רבי שמעון how offerings set aside for one occasion can be brought on another. The suggestion is that these רבנן hold the court sets conditions, even in such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: Rather, the Rabbis of "they said to him"
phrases.notes: This points to the משנה back on daf 2b, where the speakers question רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פרה proof failed, offers yet another source.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנא holds לב בית דין מתנה even for uncommon cases.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The "אמרו לו" speakers in the משנה on 2b.

steps.title: How do we know the speaker is רבי יהודה reasoning from the court's condition?
steps.stepSummary: The proof is questioned. It depends on reading the "אמרו לו" speaker as רבי יהודה, who argues from his view that the court sets conditions. The גמרא asks how we know that.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know that it is רבי יהודה, and that this is what he is saying to רבי שמעון: "Granted, according to me, since I say the court sets a condition on them, that is why they may be offered. But according to you, who say it does not, why may they be offered?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to challenge the third proof. It spells out the reading the proof depends on, that the speaker is רבי יהודה reasoning from לב בית דין מתנה, and asks how we know that. The next step offers a different reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works only if the "אמרו לו" speaker is רבי יהודה and his reason for letting the offerings be brought on another occasion is the court's condition. The גמרא asks what forces that reading. Step 6 shows the same words could come from רבי מאיר for a completely different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: from where (do you know)?
granted, it works out
the court silently sets a condition
because of this

steps.confusionAlert: The words "granted according to me… but according to you" are not the גמרא's own voice. They are what רבי יהודה might be saying to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: From where do you know that it is Rabbi Yehuda
and this is what he says to him:
Granted, according to me, since I say
the court sets a condition on them
because of that they may be offered;
but according to you, who say no
why may they be offered?

steps.triggerLanguage: ממאי דרבי יהודה היא והכי קאמר ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions who the speaker is in the source suggested in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the "אמרו לו" passage.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Nothing forces the reading that the speaker is רבי יהודה relying on the court's condition. Step 6 offers רבי מאיר instead.

steps.title: Maybe the speaker in the משנה is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The proof from 'אמרו לו' is pushed aside again. The speaker might be רבי מאיר, who allows the goats to be switched because in his view all goats atone for the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is רבי מאיר. He is saying to רבי שמעון: 'For me, since all the goats atone for the same thing, that is why they can be offered on a different occasion. But for you, who say they atone for different things, why can they be offered?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to read 'אמרו לו' so that it no longer proves anything about the court's condition. This time the speaker is רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the speaker was רבי יהודה, reasoning from the court's condition (step 5). But he might be רבי מאיר, who holds that all the goats bring the same כפרה. Then his permission to swap goats rests on that view, not on לב בית דין מתנה, so the proof for the חכמים falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a possible alternative that weakens a proof)
Granted, according to my view
Goats (here, the goat offerings of ראש חודש, the festivals and יום כיפור)
Their atonement is the same
They may be offered

phrases.english: But perhaps it is Rabbi Meir,
and this is what he is saying to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי שמעון, the one being challenged in the משנה.

phrases.english: Granted, according to me,
since I say that all the goats have the same atonement,
because of that they may be offered;
but according to you, why should they be offered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in step 5. The proof needed the speaker to be רבי יהודה, but he may be רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from 'אמרו לו' in the משנה as a source for the חכמים holding לב בית דין מתנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The speaker may be רבי מאיר, whose reason for letting the goats be swapped is that all goats atone equally. That reason has nothing to do with a court condition.
steps.whatToRemember: Three suggested sources (קטורת, פרה, "אמרו לו") have each been weakened: incense cannot graze, a heifer is expensive, and "אמרו לו" may be רבי מאיר, who allows the goats because all goats atone equally, not because of a court condition.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן had a received tradition
steps.stepSummary: Since no written source holds up, the גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן learned the dispute as a tradition. רבי שמעון says the lambs cannot be redeemed, and the חכמים say they can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן learned it as a tradition: according to רבי שמעון they are not redeemed, and according to the חכמים they are redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops searching for a written source. It says רבי יוחנן simply received this teaching from his teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three proofs (קטורת, פרה אדומה, and the goats in the משנה) were knocked down. So the חכמים' view is grounded in a tradition passed down orally, not in a passage we can point to. The ruling stands even without a written proof.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned it as a received tradition
They are redeemed (swapped for money so they lose their holiness)
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים' ruling that unneeded תמיד lambs may be redeemed (because the court sets a condition) comes from a tradition רבי יוחנן received. It is not proven from any written source.
steps.confusionAlert: 'גמרא' here does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition learned from a teacher.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן גְּמָרָא גְּמִיר לַהּ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan learned it as a tradition:
according to Rabbi Shimon, they are not redeemed,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the unblemished lambs set aside for the תמיד that weren't needed.

phrases.english: according to the Sages, they are redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן גְּמָרָא גְּמִיר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the search for a source after the last proof was rejected in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's ruling rests on a received tradition. רבי שמעון holds the lambs cannot be redeemed, and the חכמים hold they can.

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון do with the leftover lambs?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not accept the court's condition, so the lambs stay holy and cannot be redeemed. The גמרא asks what is done with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי שמעון, who does not hold that the court makes a condition on them, what do they do with them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים there is no problem, because the lambs are simply redeemed. For רבי שמעון the lambs keep their holiness and cannot be redeemed. They are also no longer needed for the תמיד, so we need to know what happens to them.

keyTerms.meaning: The court has in mind a condition on them (that they become holy only if they are needed)
What do they do with them?
He does not hold (of this idea)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon, who does not hold
that the court makes a condition about them,
what do they do with them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ לֵב בֵּית דִּין מַתְנֶה עֲלֵיהֶן מַאי עָבְדִין לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the tradition in step 7 and asks how רבי שמעון's side works in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happens, according to רבי שמעון, to unneeded תמיד lambs that cannot be redeemed.

steps.title: They are used as filler offerings for the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי יוחנן, רבי יצחק answers that the lambs are offered as extra burnt offerings at times when the מזבח would otherwise be idle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: they are used to fill in the gaps on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: This step answers the question from step 8. The leftover lambs are used for extra offerings so the מזבח is not left empty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lambs were set aside for the public as עולות, so they can still be brought as public עולות. They are brought as voluntary 'filler' offerings (קיץ המזבח) when no required offerings are scheduled. That way their holiness is used properly without redeeming them.

keyTerms.meaning: Fill in, offer as 'dessert' or filler offerings when the מזבח is idle
The altar

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
they fill in the altar with them.
phrases.notes: When no required offerings are due, these lambs are offered so the מזבח doesn't stand idle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מְקַיְּצִין בָּהֶן אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי שמעון, unneeded תמיד lambs are offered as filler burnt offerings (קיץ המזבח).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even without the court's condition, the leftover lambs are not wasted. They are used for another holy purpose.

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees that חטאת goats are not offered themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק adds a limit. Goats of a public חטאת (for example, ones that were lost and replaced) are not themselves offered as filler. Instead, their value is used to buy filler offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: רבי שמעון agrees about goats of a חטאת that the filler offerings are not brought from the animals themselves, but from their value.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher adds a limit to the rule we just learned. For חטאת goats, only their money value goes to filler offerings, not the goats themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lambs that were meant to be עולות can be offered themselves as filler עולות. A goat set aside as a חטאת is not offered itself as a filler עולה; the next step explains this is because of a גזירה of the חכמים. So it must wait until it gets a blemish, and then it is sold and the money buys filler offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (even he admits this point)
Goats brought as sin-offerings
With the animals themselves
With their value (the money they are sold for)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, leftover תמיד lambs are offered themselves as filler offerings. But with חטאת goats, only their money value is used.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
And Rabbi Shimon agrees regarding goats of a sin-offering,
that one does not fill in with the animals themselves,
but rather with their value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer in step 9 by carving out an exception for חטאת goats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רבי שמעון agrees that חטאת goats are not offered themselves as filler. Their value is used to buy filler offerings instead.

steps.title: Why lambs can be offered but sin-offering goats cannot
steps.stepSummary: The lambs started as burnt offerings and stay burnt offerings, so they can be offered directly. Goats that started as a חטאת would be switching to an עולה. A גזירה forbids this even after atonement, because of the case before atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, with the lambs, the animal was a burnt offering from the start, and now it is still a burnt offering. But there, with the goats, it was a sin offering from the start, and now it would become a burnt offering. The חכמים made a decree about after atonement because of before atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the lambs of step 9 can be offered directly, while the goats of step 10 can only have their money used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lambs never change category, because they are עולה before and עולה after. The goats would change from חטאת to עולה. Even after a replacement animal already brought the atonement, the חכמים forbade offering the goat itself, so that no one would do the same with a חטאת that has not yet atoned.

keyTerms.meaning: from the start; originally
burnt offering, fully burned on the מזבח
sin offering
a protective decree of the חכמים
atonement

steps.confusionAlert: The גזירה is not saying the goat has no atonement yet. It already did its job through the replacement animal. It is forbidden only because people might mix it up with a goat that has not yet atoned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This גזירה is the idea that אביי, רבא and רבינא now try to prove from older sources.

phrases.english: Here is where from the start it was a burnt offering
phrases.notes: "Here" means the extra lambs set aside for the תמיד. "There" means the goats of a public חטאת.

phrases.english: and now it is a burnt offering;
but there, where from the start it was a sin offering
and now it would be a burnt offering –
there is a decree regarding after atonement
because of before atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא הוּא דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא עוֹלָה וְהַשְׁתָּא עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the limit stated in step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If lambs can be offered directly as filler, goats of a public חטאת should be offered directly too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Goats that started as a חטאת fall under a גזירה, made after atonement because of before atonement, so only their money is used.

steps.title: אביי brings a ברייתא about lost public sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא. The lost bull and goat of יום הכפורים, and the lost goats of עבודה זרה, were replaced and later found. רבי יהודה says they are left to die. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say they graze until blemished, and their money goes to gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learned this in a ברייתא. A bull and goat of יום הכפורים were lost, and others were set aside in their place. Likewise, goats for a communal mistake in idol worship were lost, and others were set aside in their place. In all these cases the originals must die, according to רבי יהודה. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: they graze until they get a blemish, then they are sold and the money goes to gift offerings, because a public sin offering is not left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא that he thinks supports the גזירה. This step quotes the source, and the next step will show how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is exactly our case: a public חטאת whose atonement was already done by a replacement. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say these animals should not die. But they also do not say to offer them directly. Instead, they must wait for a blemish and then be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: we too have learned this (in an older source)
they are left to die
they graze until they get a blemish
gift offering, here meaning public offerings bought with the money
a sin offering of the whole community

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: אביי said: We too have learned this:
the bull and goat of יום הכפורים
that were lost, and he set aside others in their place,
and likewise the goats for idol worship
phrases.notes: These are goats the community brings when it worshipped idols by mistake.

phrases.english: that were lost, and he set aside others in their place –
all of them must be left to die. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say:
they should graze until they become blemished,
and then they are sold, and their money goes to gift offerings;
because a public sin offering is not left to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an older source to support the גזירה of step 11
steps.raayaObject: The גזירה forbidding a public חטאת to be offered directly as an עולה after atonement
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר with רבי שמעון about lost public sin offerings

steps.title: אביי shows how the ברייתא proves the decree
steps.stepSummary: Why do רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון make the animals wait for a blemish instead of offering them directly as an עולה? It must be because of the גזירה made after atonement because of before atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let the animals themselves be offered as a burnt offering! Rather, must we not learn from this that there is a decree about after atonement because of before atonement?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the proof. The ברייתא's ruling only makes sense if there is a גזירה against offering the animal itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law these leftover animals could be offered directly as filler burnt offerings. The ברייתא instead requires a long wait for a blemish and a sale. That roundabout path shows the חכמים forbade offering the animal itself.

keyTerms.meaning: why?
they themselves (the animals themselves)
learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא never mentions offering the animal itself, only selling it after a blemish. אביי reads that silence as proof of the גזירה.

phrases.english: But why?
Let the animals themselves be offered as a burnt offering!
Rather, must we not learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵירָה לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה אַטּוּ לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה?
phrases.english: there is a decree regarding after atonement because of before atonement?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 12 proves the גזירה
steps.raayaObject: The גזירה made after atonement because of before atonement
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון require waiting for a blemish instead of offering the animal directly

steps.title: רבא brings support from a משנה about the יום הכפורים goats
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה: the extra second goat grazes until it gets a blemish, and then it is sold and its money goes to gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We also learned this in a משנה: and the second goat grazes until it gets a blemish, then it is sold and its money goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second source for the same idea. Here he only quotes the משנה, and the explanation of the proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה, like the ברייתא, has a leftover public חטאת goat. It sends the goat to graze and be sold, not to be offered directly as an עולה. רבא sees this as more support for the גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: the second one (the extra goat)
it is sold

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: רבא said: We too have learned this:
and the second one grazes until it becomes blemished,
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה in יומא about the יום הכפורים goats. "The second" is a leftover goat that is no longer needed.

phrases.english: and it is sold, and its money goes to gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate proof for the same גזירה, from a משנה instead of a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: The גזירה forbidding a leftover public חטאת to be offered directly as an עולה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in יומא about the extra יום הכפורים goat

steps.title: Why not offer the extra goat itself?
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his proof. The משנה should have let the extra goat be offered as an עולה, but it did not. So there must be a גזירה after atonement because of before atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why wait for a blemish? Let the goat itself be offered as a burnt offering! Rather, must we not learn from this that there is a decree after atonement because of before atonement?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how the משנה from step 14 proves the rule of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes the extra goat wait for a blemish and only uses its money. The easier path would be to offer the goat itself as an עולה. The only reason not to do that is the גזירה: an animal that started as a חטאת may not become an עולה, even after atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule the Rabbis made to protect against a mistake
Atonement; the moment the owner is forgiven through the offering
Itself; the animal itself, not its money
Because of; on account of a different case

phrases.english: But why? Let the animal itself be offered as a burnt offering!
phrases.notes: He means the extra goat from the משנה in step 14.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵרָה אַחַר כַּפָּרָה אַטּוּ לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה?
phrases.english: a decree after atonement, because of before atonement?
phrases.notes: After atonement it would be fine by itself. Before atonement it is still a real חטאת, so the חכמים forbade both cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's proof that began with the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The rule of רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק and the גזירה after atonement because of before atonement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that says the extra goat grazes until it gets a blemish (step 14).

steps.title: רבינא brings a third source: a משנה about a guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes a משנה about an אשם whose owner died or already got atonement. The animal grazes until blemished and its money goes to gift offerings. רבי אליעזר says it dies. רבי יהושע says its money buys an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We also learned this in a משנה. A guilt offering whose owner died, or whose owner already got atonement, should graze until it gets a blemish. Then it is sold and its money goes to gift offerings. רבי אליעזר says: It should die. רבי יהושע says: He should bring a burnt offering with its money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a second משנה that can prove the same גזירה. Here he only quotes the source. The proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is about an אשם, not a חטאת, but the question is the same: can a leftover sin-type offering become an עולה? Look closely at all three opinions. None of them says to offer the animal itself. Even רבי יהושע only uses its money.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
Its owner, the person who brought the offering
Becomes unfit, meaning it gets a blemish
Its money, the value it is sold for
Gift offerings bought with community money

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבִינָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Ravina said: We too have learned it in a Mishnah:
A guilt offering whose owner died
or whose owner already got atonement
should graze until it gets a blemish,
and then be sold, and its money goes to gift offerings.
Rabbi Eliezer says: It should be left to die.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יָבִיא בְּדָמָיו עוֹלָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: He should bring a burnt offering with its money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof from a different משנה, alongside רבא's proof.
steps.raayaObject: The גזירה after atonement because of before atonement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about a leftover אשם.

steps.title: The guilt offering proves the decree
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks why the אשם itself is not offered as an עולה. The only answer is the גזירה after atonement because of before atonement. The גמרא agrees: learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let this animal itself be offered as a burnt offering! Rather, is it not because of a decree after atonement, because of before atonement? Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא draws the proof out of the משנה he just quoted, and the גמרא accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If offering the leftover אשם as an עולה were allowed, someone in the משנה would have said so. Instead, every opinion avoids offering the animal itself. That silence shows a גזירה is in place, and the words שמע מינה close the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be offered
Learn from it; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: Two משניות (the extra goat and the leftover אשם) both show the same thing. An animal that started as a sin-type offering is never offered directly as an עולה, even after atonement. Only its money is used, because of the גזירה.

phrases.english: But let this animal itself be offered as a burnt offering!
Rather, is it not a decree after atonement
because of before atonement? Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 16 and confirms it.
steps.raayaObject: The גזירה after atonement because of before atonement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the leftover אשם, where no opinion offers the animal itself.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The גזירה is confirmed: a former אשם or חטאת is not offered as an עולה even after atonement.

steps.title: A ברייתא about leftover lambs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a ברייתא that supports the earlier teaching. It asks what offerings were brought from the leftover lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: What do they bring from the leftovers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a supporting source. It quotes only the opening question of a ברייתא, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier רבי יוחנן said that, according to רבי שמעון, leftover lambs are offered directly as filler offerings for the מזבח (step 9). This ברייתא will back up that point by telling us exactly what was done with them.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא; a supporting source
Leftovers, extra animals that were not used

phrases.english: It was also taught this way in a Baraita:
What do they bring from the leftovers?
phrases.notes: These are the leftover lambs set aside for the daily offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the גזירה proofs and returns to the earlier point about leftover lambs.
steps.raayaObject: The earlier teaching that leftover lambs are offered directly as filler offerings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about what is brought from the leftovers (its answer continues on the next amud).
